x: It would be very nice to see Ted Gaworski and Dick Harris reach 50 feet and over in the weight. I am happy that Mal Ash will be giving us his valuable support this year. Percy Luxon - what about 24 feet this year.

Percy Luxon won the Long Jump with 22 feet 11 inches and Mal Ash was second in the High Jump. Percy Porter deserves special mention for setting a new club record in the hammer throw at Eton Manor with 166 feet 9ins.
Mal Ash gave us third place in the 120 yards hurdles and Dennis Merrett was a comfortable winner of the 220 hurdles. The 440 yards hurdles was the only event in which we did not score points.

They were George Williams 3rd in the two miles walk (14.51.6), Mal Ash 2nd in the High Jump (5' 11") and R.J. Harris 4th in the Shot (48' 5") In addition Stan Vickers represented Kent in the 7 miles Walk and finished 4th in 52.19.4 in one of the finest races at this distance in post war years.

Mal Ash gained a standard in the heats of the 120yds hurdles qualifying for the final in 15.6 and was 4th in the final.. Alan Sexton had to be content with a Southern Standard in the 440 but I think we can expect a return to his old form before long.
Percy Luxon retained his title in the Long Jump with a leap of 22ft. 10ins. Mal Ash was 2nd and D.

Mal Ash had a fall in the heat of the 120 yards hurdles when nicely placed and might well have done his best to date. Our team in the 4 x 110 yards Junior Relay were well beaten in their heat mainly through poor baton changing and our hopes of seeing Belgrave colours to the fore were once again dashed.

Jones ran exceedingly well to gain 2nd and 4th places in the sprints. Mal Ash was second in the 120 yards hurdles and Percy Porter 5th. Alan Sexton won the 440 yards hurdles in 49.7secs. a grand performance.

Here again lads doubled up and even did three events to try and gain points Mal Ash won the high jump and Long Jump with Adjei 2nd. This last addition from the Gold Coast should be an asset when he settles down.
Jones was in great form and broke the ground record for the shot put with 47ft. 1in. Mal Ash won the high jump and just failed to equal the ground record.

Just in time for inclusion in this issue is the success of our versatile field events member Mal Ash who on 8th September won the Southern Decathalon with a total score of 5,178 points, 543 points more than the 2nd man.

Mal Ash won the pole vault, high jump and 120yds. hurdles and was placed in the triple jump- what an asset this boy is! John Davies won the 800 metres in 1m.57.6s. whilst Gerry Leroy was unlucky not get into the final.
John's time was 1min.55.8secs, truly wonderful running on such a cold night. Our field events lads performed well, M.

Roy Liggins 2nd in the Javelin was a good effort, as was that of promising new member Ware in 6th place. Mal Ash only did two events, getting a 1st and 2nd, and Charlie Jones also got a double of "sorts".
Whilst this was going on Mal Ash had started a long effort in the Pole Vault. He was not in such good form as last year but secured fourth place with 12'0" - losing third only on failures.

… Whilst Morris, who is now a recruit at the Police Training School scored 4th place for the police. In the field events Mal Ash and P.Luxon secured maximum points for us in the long jump with 22'1" and 21'10" respectively.…
I should be interested to learn Mal Ash's heat time in the Kinnaird, or in the final if his time was taken. I think it likely he beat his Club record of 15.4 sec.
(1) With the exception of Mal Ash, no person's name appears more than twice in any age-group. (2) Alan Sexton is the only Junior record holder who also holds a senior record.

We had successes in a number of County championships but "Iron Man" Mal Ash had a slightly disappointing season. Mal Ash collected his usual quota of points with a win in the High Jump (5'7") and a second in the pole vault(11'6"). Three Bels supported Mal in the high jump with 5'6", 5'4" and 5'0"; the latter performance by Roach, still only a boy.
The field events saw a welcome return to competition of Mal Ash who won the long jump with 20'6" and finished third in the javelin,with 135'5" behind Bill Couzens who threw 142'5".

Norman Caves won the hop, step and jump with 43'3" while in the pole vault Mal Ash did well to secure fourth place. Our track runners were more numerous, although in some of the events they were completely outclassed, notably the 880 yds, in which P.

There were, however, some good individual performances by Club members and the following are on record:- 440 yds in 49.6s. by Brian Morris, 1 mile in 4m.11.6s. by John Davies and a 5'10" high jump and a 21'10½" long jump by Mal Ash.
High Jump · M.C. Ash · 6' 1"
Tolson had pulled a muscle, Norman Caves had contracted tonsilitis, Andorka was sitting very important exams and Mal Ash threatened to retire; I was unable to change his mind.

Jim McGrath, our new member from Northern Ireland who seems to be another Mal Ash, jumped a most creditable 21'0" to finish 5th. The junior sprints illustrated our sad lack of young sprinters but this was offset to some extent by the promising debut of Linley in the 440 yds.

McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave.
Jim McGrath is another "Iron Man" of the calibre of Mal Ash. His efforts in two, three or even four events at matches has been of inestimable help and in true Belgrave Spirit.

Set up in Vancouver Trophy meeting when winning his event. Beats Mal Ash's 5 yr old record by one tenth of a second.

Trevor, who first gained an A.A.A. vest 10 years ago, says he will keep at it until he breaks that magical 15 seconds. Incidentally, his time of 15.2 sets a new club record - improving by one-fifth of a second on Mal Ash's mark set in 1955.

However, that oft - repeated maxim "success breeds success" could easily be set in motion should we discover another Mal Ash or a Jim McGrath.

29th June: John Martin,who is following in the footsteps of ex-Belgravian Mal Ash, had no difficulty in winning the Discus after already competing in two other events.New members Frank Glass and Dennis Gleeson also performed well,the latter looking as if he could well be a member of our winning team…

In winning the High Jump with a personal best of 6'0", Barry Townsend became the first Belgravian to clear this height since Mal Ash in 1958 .

From Australia we had a great all-rounder Mal Ash who did the Decathlon, with the High Jump, Pole Vault and Hurdles as his strong events. Although he didn't reach his best with us Gordon Mackenzie, a 10,000 metres and marathon runner, subsequently represented the U.S.A. in the 1960 Olympic Games.
